title: Externalize trace metadata to reduce hotpath allocations
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: high-allocation tracing hotpath in the inference ingress and runtime proxies is increasing GC pressure and CPU on critical low-latency paths. Current instrumentation materializes per-request attribute maps (user metadata, route tags, sampling hints) inline on the hotpath, even for traces that will be sampled out, leading to O(4-12KB) allocations per request in high-QPS services.

Proposal: introduce an externalized, append-only trace-metadata store (lightweight sidecar + in-memory LRU index) and change hotpath tracing to emit a compact metadata token (8-16 bytes) instead of a full attribute map. The full attribute blob is written to the metadata store asynchronously when necessary (on sampled traces, on-demand tail analysis). The metadata store will expose a small HTTP/gRPC fetch API used by offline tail analyzers and the tracing backend. We will also implement a compact binary attribute encoding and a fast tokenization step to minimize encoding cost on the hotpath.

Scope: ingress proxies, runtime fronting layer, and SDK hotpath instrumentation. This change targets allocation reduction and CPU savings without altering trace semantics for sampled traces.

Risks and tradeoffs: additional component (sidecar) increases system complexity and failure surface; need to ensure metadata store availability and bounded memory (LRU + TTL). Must design for multi-tenant isolation and encryption-at-rest for any persisted blobs. We will mitigate with graceful degradation (fall back to inline attributes if store unavailable) and strict size limits per-blob.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath per-request heap allocations reduced by >=65% in measured services (target: drop from ~6KB to <=2KB per request)
End-to-end p50 CPU for ingress process improves by >=3% under representative synthetic load
No loss of sampled trace fidelity: traces sampled 1% must be reconstructable with attribute blobs fetched from the metadata store
Graceful degradation path implemented and exercised: if metadata service is unreachable, instrumentation falls back to inline attribute emission and emits a warning metric
Add dashboard panels showing metadata-store hit/miss rate, average blob size, and tokenization latency; integrate alerts if miss rate >1% or average blob >32KB
comments: 2025-01-15 Ava Martinez: Triage - flagged as follow-up to ongoing tracing cost initiative. Impact: medium; aligns with runtime-1.20 planning.

2025-01-20 Liam Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype sidecar and token emission in the test SDK. Raw results: allocations dropped ~68% in the minimal proxy benchmark (qps=4k). Attached perf graphs in the design doc.
2025-01-22 Priya Desai (review): Concerned about multi-tenant blob sizes and KMS costs. Suggested adding per-tenant blob caps and optional compression. Also asked for failure-mode testing plan.
2025-01-27 Liam Chen: Added TTL and LRU in-memory index. Compression enabled for blobs >1KB (snappy). Updated runbook with fallback flow when sidecar returns 5xx.

2025-01-30 QA: Load test (inference-proxy) at qps=10k for 15m. Observed tokenization latency median 80us, p99 220us. Metadata store avg write latency 4ms (with batch write coalescing). Blob miss rate <0.2%.

2025-02-03 Security (Maya Patel): Reviewed encryption and tenant isolation. Requested KMS envelope encryption for persisted blobs and audit logging on fetch operations. Marked security_review_required true for enterprise private deployments.

2025-02-05 Design review: Decided to gate change behind a feature flag per-service. Will rollout in 3 stages: (1) opt-in sidecar, (2) default enabled for non-critical internal tenants, (3) enable for production with SLO guardrails. Added metrics to the rollout plan.
2025-02-06 Liam Chen: Preparing PR for upstream SDK. Next: implement per-blob size rejection path and update console dashboards. Scheduling canary for 2025-02-12.
implementation_notes: Server-side: lightweight sidecar (Go) with in-memory LRU index and append-only on-disk segments for durability. Client-side: tokenization is a two-step fast path: 1) try small inline key-value compact encoding (if attributes <=64 bytes) else 2) asynchronously POST blob to sidecar and synchronously emit token referencing current segment+offset. Instrumentation emits a metric trace.metadata.tokenize.latency. Rollout behind feature flag: tracing.metadata.externalization.
notes_for_oncall: If metadata-store alert fires (miss rate >1% or write error rate >0.5%), oncall should flip feature flag to disable externalization for affected services and follow runbook at https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/trace-metadata-sidecar.md
